references.text: Matthew's parallel account of the storm on the sea, where Jesus sleeps in the boat while a violent storm breaks out and the disciples wake him in fear.
Mark's parallel account of the storm on the Sea of Galilee, where Jesus sleeps on a cushion in the boat while a fierce storm fills the boat with water.
Jonah experienced a similar situation when he slept during a violent storm at sea, while the ship was in danger of sinking.
The psalm describes those who go out to sea and encounter storms and danger, where waves rise up and they are in great distress—a thematic parallel to the disciples' situation on the sea.
The psalmist cries out to God who seems to be asleep and asks him to wake up, a parallel to the disciples waking the sleeping Jesus during the storm.
The psalmist's cry that the waters threaten to overwhelm him and that he is sinking reflects the life-threatening danger the disciples faced when the boat was filled with water.
A call for the Lord's arm to awake, referencing God's power over the depths of the sea—a thematic parallel to Jesus being awakened and demonstrating power over the storm.
